galleryFloorCoverageDescriptionProposed: Six connected spaces: great room, kitchen, formal dining, piano salon, sunroom and stair hall, each with two daytime angles and matching night views. Dining and living share a continuous oak floor, flat ceiling and five-opening east facade; the living north wall is solid behind its exterior false-window feature. Original photos anchor visible architecture; salon and alternate-camera details follow the builder plan. Companion angles do not survey every unseen wall. Field measurements and one coordinated furniture/window-treatment plan govern fit and construction.

sourceFacts.adjacency: Living is NORTH of formal dining, and dining is SOUTH of living. Their shared boundary is an imaginary furniture-zone line, not a wall or opening cut through a wall. The printed plan shows no partition, column, arch, door, header, threshold or elevation change at that boundary.
sourceFacts.openBoundary: Keep the complete adjoining boundary open across the overlapping room depth. The west-side hall/stair approach also flows into the front rooms. The two-story entry void and butler pantry constrain the dining's western side; the stair well constrains the living's northwest approach. Do not replace these relationships with a separate boxed piano room or a grand framed portal.
sourceFacts.westHall: Living's west/hall edge flows openly beside the stairwell guard. The stair photograph's arch connects farther west to the great room, while the plan also labels a separate dining-to-butler-pantry arch on the dining's west side. Neither arch belongs on the living/dining seam. A tighter LR2 diagonal toward dining avoids inventing unseen distant hall/ceiling details.
sourceFacts.livingWindows: Exactly TWO real tall narrow windows on the living's EAST exterior wall, printed bottom/right portion. Their positions follow the plan. No floor-to-ceiling slider, third tall living window or wraparound corner glazing.
sourceFacts.northWall: The printed right/north facade feature is explicitly labeled 'False Window'. It is not an interior opening. Keep this wall solid inside, particularly behind/near the piano. Do not give it drapes, glass, a niche or an exterior view.
sourceFacts.sharedEastElevation: Two dining tall windows, then a small high arched window near the dining/living junction, then two living tall windows. The high window does not become a third full-height living window. In the original dining photo, the screen-left wall is this east elevation: the small high arched window and two tall rectangular windows with slim rectangular transoms. The screen-right wall is the south facade with two arched-top dining windows.
sourceFacts.livingGlazingType: Use tall narrow rectangular double-hung windows with light inner trim and a slim rectangular transom treatment consistent with the adjoining east-wall dining windows and actual exterior. Exact unseen interior living trim/sash detail remains inferred; do not claim it is verified by a dedicated room photograph.
sourceFacts.ceiling: Original adjoining dining photograph has a flat ceiling, perimeter crown and discreet recessed fixtures. Keep one continuous flat plane between living and dining, with no dropped beam, portal header, isolated ceiling box, tray, cove or seam introduced between furniture zones.
sourceFacts.floor: One continuous natural matte oak floor through both zones, same direction/color/level. Loose rugs can define furniture groups; no threshold, border strip, step or flooring material change at the open boundary.

furniturePlan.piano: Compact baby grand around 5 feet long, in the northwestern living corner beside the solid north wall/stair-side return, as the plan's piano placement indicates. Angle keyboard toward the room/dining; allow a real bench and playing space. Keep it away from direct east-window sun and outside the hall/dining circulation route.
furniturePlan.sofa: One appropriately scaled ivory RH Cloud-style sofa, approximately 8 to 9 feet wide and standard depth, along the east-window side facing west into the salon. Do not insert a broad sofa-backed barrier across the entire shared dining boundary. No oversized U-shaped media-room arrangement here.
furniturePlan.table: Compact walnut coffee table and oatmeal loose rug within the seating group. Supporting lounge chair is optional only if a measured furniture plan confirms circulation; do not add it merely to fill the rendering.
furniturePlan.circulation: Show an obvious uninterrupted walk from the west hall/stair approach into both living and dining and between the piano bench and seating. Target at least about 36 inches for the main furniture circulation route where feasible; this is design intent, not a verified field clearance or code determination. Furniture, lid and bench cannot consume the route.
furniturePlan.finishes: Original Mineral & Walnut: warm neutral mineral walls, natural oak floor, walnut supporting table, ivory upholstery and sheers, restrained black piano/art/lighting and green plants. No blue/yellow/chrome Option 2 palette.

fieldMeasurementCaveat: All renders are design visualizations. Builder plan labels, photographic perspectives and pixel ratios do not establish exact opening offsets, rise/going, service locations, clear dimensions, furniture fit, piano weight/delivery or cabinetry fabrication. Confirm actual room/window/stair measurements, product footprints, chair pullback, piano lid/bench space, privacy sightlines, substrate, lighting/dimming and installation systems before procurement or construction.
